newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: CRICKET-SIDHU CENTURY PUTS INDIA ON PUT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SIDHU CENTURY PUTS INDIA ON PUT.

text.p: A century by opener Navjot Sidhu put India on top on the second day of the second test on Saturday after they had earlier bowled out the West Indies for 296.
By the close, India were 171 for one in reply to the West Indies first innings total in which Roland Holder came within nine runs of his maiden test century.

Sidhu, on his first overseas assignment since walking out on the India squad in England last year, finally found his form after a poor first test in which he scored only 10 runs in the two innings combined.

Sidhu and partner Rahul Dravid, with a half century, frustrated West Indies with an unbroken 171 partnership after India had lost opener Vangipurappu Laxman for a duck when he was lbw to Curtley Ambrose on the second ball of the innings.

At the close Sidhu was not out 102 and Dravid 57. India will now be looking to a similar performance from captain Sachin Tendulkar, who like Sidhu, failed in to make an impact in the drawn first test in Jamaica.

India, playing on the ground where they recorded their last test victory in the Caribbean 21 years ago, had earlier polished off the West Indian batsmen after the home team had resumed on an overnight total of 239 for seven.
Barbadian Roland Holder fell for 91 before the West Indies lost their last three wickets for just seven runs.
Holder, 71 overnight, was bowled leg stump by left-arm spinner Sunil Joshi after a 239-ball innings lasting 293 minutes with seven fours.

Captain Courtney Walsh was next out, caught behind off Saurav Ganguly without scoring after facing just three balls. Fast bowler Franklyn Rose struck 34, including two sixes and two fours and shared in a stand of 69 with Holder, a West Indies' eighth-wicket record against India.
Leg-spinner Anil Kumble captured five for 104 off 38 overs, all of them on Friday, with Joshi taking three for 79. Kumble has so far taken 13 wickets in the series.
